newsitem.title: NORWAY: Elkem to raise silicon metal output.
newsitem.headline: Elkem to raise silicon metal output.

text.p: Norwegian metals maker Elkem ASA said on Friday it planned to increase silicon metal output by 20,000 tonnes a year at Elkem Alloy in West Virginia.
Elkem said in a statement it would increase capacity at Elkem Alloy by resuming production at furnace no. 15.
"The investment in Alloy is a step in Elkem's strategy to strengthen its role as the world's largest producer of silicon metal," the statement said.
"The new furnace combined with increased production at the plant's four other silicon metal furnaces will increase production at Elkem Alloy by 20,000 tonnes annually."
"Furnace no. 15 will enter production in the second quarter of 1998. The investment is conditional of obligatory approvals based on environmental considerations," it said.
Elkem said last year it covers 18 percent of the world market for silicon metals, which are used for microchips in personal computers and other sophisticated products.
It said the computer and communications industry is a rapidly growing market for silicon metal.
